title: Read It Back: Pretrained MLLMs Are Zero-Shot Reward Models for Text-to-Image Generation
task: Reward modeling for text-to-image generation RL without training
key_results: SpectraReward improves generation across two diffusion models and three RL algorithms; Self-SpectraReward matches larger external reward models, indicating reward-policy alignment is key
comments: Elegant approach leveraging pretrained MLLM alignment via prompt recovery, though the claim that larger reward models aren't always better warrants investigation into why scaling breaks reward quality.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Image-conditioned prompt recovery provides effective reward signal without fine-tuning
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; SpectraReward consistently improves across benchmarks

hypotheses.hypothesis: Larger reward MLLMs always perform better
hypotheses.result: Rejected; no monotonic relationship between model size and reward quality

title: SynthDocBench: Controlled Benchmark for Long-Context Visual Document Understanding
task: Controlled evaluation of VLM long-context visual document understanding
key_results: Uncovered sharp degradation with document length, middle-third positional sensitivity (8.3pp decline), and chart comprehension breakdown; frontier models score 21-28/100 on long documents
comments: Synthetic benchmarks with controlled factors are valuable but may not fully capture real-world document complexity and user intent variations.

inputs: synthetic long documents with varying length/layout/modality

hypotheses.hypothesis: VLMs degrade predictably with document length
hypotheses.result: confirmed - sharp degradation observed

hypotheses.hypothesis: Model performance is uniform across document positions
hypotheses.result: rejected - middle third systematically harder for 5/6 models

title: Blind-Spots-Bench: Evaluating Blind Spots in Multimodal Models
task: Identifying blind spots in multimodal AI models
key_results: Closed-source frontier models outperform open-weight by ~10% despite comparable established-benchmark performance; no single model dominates across task types
comments: A valuable diagnostic tool revealing capability gaps, though 235 samples is relatively modest for deep model characterization and the student-sourced task distribution may skew toward certain problem types.

model_io.model: Language, vision-language, and image-generation models (open and closed)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Frontier closed-source models have fewer blind spots than open-weight peers
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; ~10% performance gap observed

hypotheses.hypothesis: Single best model exists across all task types
hypotheses.result: Rejected; capability varies by task category

title: Search Beyond What Can Be Taught: Evolving the Knowledge Boundary in Agentic Visual Generation
task: Agentic visual generation with world-knowledge grounding via search
key_results: Frontier generators collapse from benchmark performance to 21-28/100 on knowledge-grounded requests; teach-then-search co-training produces monotonic improvement
comments: The identified knowledge boundary is model-specific and evolving, making the co-training discovery approach pragmatic but potentially difficult to scale across different generators.

model_io.model: frontier open visual generators + search agents

hypotheses.hypothesis: Naive search improves visual generation for out-of-distribution requests
hypotheses.result: rejected - naive search injects noise and fails indiscriminately

hypotheses.hypothesis: Co-training discovers generator-specific knowledge boundaries
hypotheses.result: confirmed - teach-then-search framework enables recursive improvement

title: Know Before Fix: QA-Driven Repository Knowledge Acquisition for Software Issue Resolution
task: Automated software issue resolution via QA-driven knowledge acquisition
key_results: ACQUIRE raises Pass@1 by up to 4.4 percentage points on SWE-bench Verified compared to pre-repair methods
comments: Principled decoupling of comprehension from action mirrors sound engineering practice, though modest gains and added computational cost suggest incremental rather than transformative impact.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Explicit knowledge acquisition before repair outperforms implicit fix-driven exploration
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; consistent improvements over pre-repair baselines

title: MuScriptor: An Open Model for Multi-Instrument Music Transcription
task: Multi-instrument music transcription from real recordings
key_results: MuScriptor combines synthetic pretraining, real-music fine-tuning, and RL post-training; works on diverse genre mixes and supports instrument-presence conditioning
comments: Practical open-weight contribution addressing a real generalization challenge, but abstract lacks quantitative metrics (e.g., accuracy, word-error rate) making impact assessment difficult.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Synthetic pretraining + real fine-tuning + RL improves multi-instrument transcription generalization
hypotheses.result: Supported (abstract does not quantify explicitly, but model release and genre diversity suggest success)

title: Let RGB Be the Language of Vision
task: Unified vision model via RGB in-and-out formulation for diverse visual tasks
key_results: Single model achieves competitive zero-shot performance on both dense understanding (segmentation, depth) and dense-conditioned generation (pose-to-image) without task-specific fine-tuning
comments: RGB encoding of structured outputs (masks, depth) is elegant but may lose semantic information; generalization to more complex visual phenomena needs validation.

inputs: structured visual signals (masks, depth as RGB)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Diverse visual tasks can be unified via RGB-to-RGB formulation
hypotheses.result: confirmed - single model handles segmentation, depth, pose-to-image zero-shot

title: MonkeyOCRv2: A Visual-Text Foundation Model for Document AI
task: Document-oriented visual-text pretraining for document AI tasks
key_results: MonkeyOCRv2 0.7B frozen encoder surpasses 3B baseline by 2.8% on MDPBench; improves five document analysis tasks consistently; outperforms CLIP/DINO/SAM on document understanding
comments: Document-specific pretraining is effective but the comparison to CLIP/DINO (natural image models) may not be entirely fair; generalization to non-document visual tasks unstated.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Character-level visual perception improves document image analysis
hypotheses.result: confirmed - consistent improvements across text recognition, detection, tampering, segmentation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Document-pretrained encoder outperforms natural-image pretraining for document tasks

key_results: Asymptotic RL performance shows non-monotone relationship between rankings and data regimes; prior research under canonical paradigms reached incorrect conclusions

title: Bridging the translational gap in radiotherapy: a human three-dimensional cell culture for evaluating neutron biological effects
task: Evaluate neutron radiation relative biological effectiveness (RBE) in 3D tissue models versus 2D cultures
key_results: 3D models show lower radiation sensitivity than 2D monolayers, better matching clinical tissue resistance
Dose-dependent extracellular matrix thinning observed at ≥25 Gy in neutron-irradiated 3D tissues
comments: The shift from 2D to 3D culture for RBE assessment is practically important for clinical translation, though the mechanistic basis for differential sensitivity and the relationship between ECM damage and cell death remain incompletely characterized.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Neutron damage includes structural ECM injury beyond cell death
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: dose-dependent ECM thinning at high doses independent of cell viability endpoints

title: Modular in vivo antibody–ADC click to reverse drug resistance in tumours
task: Overcome ADC resistance in heterogeneous tumors through in vivo bioorthogonal antibody-ADC assembly
key_results: Improved antitumor activity versus standard ADC monotherapy in HER2/EGFR co-expressing tumors; efficacy in low, ultralow, negative or heterogeneous antigen expression settings
comments: Elegant use of click chemistry to bypass single-antigen dependency, though clinical translation of in vivo ligation timing and efficiency remains to be demonstrated.

title: Multiomic profiling of responses to clinical and novel bisphosphonates reveals extraskeletal effects on ageing related signatures
task: Identify geroprotective mechanisms of bisphosphonates in non-skeletal tissues via multiomic profiling
key_results: Spatial transcriptomics in aged mice treated with zoledronate shows shift toward young cellular composition in heart, liver, intestine with upregulated detoxification, mitochondrial stability, and antioxidation genes; proteomic analysis shows ~400 protein alterations with downregulation of aging hallmarks; low-dose BPs stimulate growth and protect against senescence via MEF2A; previously unrecognized targets include PHB2 and ASAH1
comments: Surprising geroprotective extra-skeletal effects of clinically-used BPs; multi-tissue and mechanistic dissection reveals actionable pathways independent of bone effects.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bisphosphonates exert geroprotective effects in non-skeletal tissues via altered gene expression and protein signatures

hypotheses.hypothesis: MEF2A mediates zoledronate-triggered geroprotection in cardiomyocytes
hypotheses.result: Validated as key mediator through proteome-wide target deconvolution; low BP doses protect cardiomyocytes against DNA damage-induced senescence

title: Novel nuclear RNA export factor 1 adaptor drives tumor growth by increasing proliferation-stimulatory mRNA export
task: Identify PANAD as novel NXF1 adaptor driving HCC proliferation via mRNA export
key_results: PANAD (C7orf25/proliferation-associated NXF1 adaptor) interacts with NXF1 RBD via R122/E125/G133/D139, disrupting intramolecular RBD-NTF2L interaction and enhancing mRNA binding; PANAD knockdown impairs export of proliferation-pathway mRNAs including CDK6; PANAD accelerates G1/S transition, promotes xenograft growth; upregulated in HCC tissues; PANAD-overexpressing cells show increased CDK4/6 inhibitor sensitivity
comments: Novel mechanistic role for previously uncharacterized protein in NXF1 adaptor landscape; PANAD serves as both therapeutic target and CDK4/6 inhibitor response biomarker.

hypotheses.hypothesis: PANAD disrupts NXF1 intramolecular interaction to enhance mRNA binding and export

hypotheses.hypothesis: PANAD selectively enhances export of proliferation-stimulatory mRNAs including CDK6
hypotheses.result: PANAD knockdown impairs nuclear export of proliferation-pathway mRNAs; PANAD binds CDK6 mRNA directly

hypotheses.hypothesis: PANAD overexpression sensitizes cells to CDK4/6 inhibitors
hypotheses.result: PANAD-overexpressing cells show increased palbociclib sensitivity; PANAD-silenced cells show reduced sensitivity

title: BAP1 deficiency-induced SKA3 promotes clear cell renal cell carcinoma malignant progression by regulating chromosomal instability
task: Establish BAP1-SKA3 axis as CIN driver in ccRCC
key_results: BAP1 mutations drive aberrant SKA3 overexpression; BAP1 deubiquitinates NCOR1 to repress SKA3 and deubiquitinates H2AK119 to activate TRIM25 (degrades SKA3); BAP1 deficiency disrupts both pathways; SKA3 accumulation correlates with metastasis and poor prognosis
comments: Dual regulatory mechanisms (transcriptional and post-translational) provide mechanistic redundancy; elegant integration of histone and non-histone deubiquitination.

hypotheses.hypothesis: BAP1 loss drives aberrant SKA3 overexpression through dual regulatory pathways
hypotheses.result: NCOR1 deubiquitination-mediated transcriptional repression and TRIM25-mediated ubiquitin-proteasome degradation both disrupted in BAP1-deficient cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: SKA3 accumulation drives CIN and correlates with poor prognosis

title: Remodeling of ferroptotic necroinflammation by dexamethasone in acute tubular necrosis
task: Define ferroptotic necroinflammation remodeling by dexamethasone in acute tubular necrosis
key_results: Dexamethasone shows biphasic ferroptosis effect: early sensitization via glutathione depletion followed by resistance via GR1-mediated ferrous iron reduction; attenuates tubular injury but worsens renal function through enhanced innate immune recruitment; demonstrates temporally opposing ferroptotic modulatory effects
comments: Sophisticated mechanistic example of pleiotropic glucocorticoid signaling; highlights complexity of necroinflammation where ferroptosis modulation and immune effects diverge.

model_io.model: Renal tubular cells and tissues (acute tubular necrosis context)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dexamethasone exhibits biphasic ferroptosis effect with early sensitization and later resistance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed with initial glutathione-depletion sensitization followed by iron-limiting resistance

hypotheses.hypothesis: GR1-mediated iron reduction mediates ferroptosis resistance but has ferroptosis-independent immunological consequences
hypotheses.result: Dexamethasone reduces ferrous iron and attenuates tubular injury but enhances innate immune recruitment worsening renal function

comments: Novel selectivity mechanism exploiting ALT-specific Rad51 dependence; APB localization of RFWD3-mediated degradation is a clever therapeutic vulnerability.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Wi-A selectively impairs ALT cancer cells by disrupting Rad51-dependent HR

title: Exogenous creatine supplementation promotes tumor metastasis via megakaryocyte creatine kinase B-STAT5B signaling
task: Elucidate creatine-mediated tumor metastasis mechanism
key_results: Creatine supplementation increases platelet activation via megakaryocyte CKB-STAT5B signaling; Slc6a8 or Stat5b knockout ablates metastasis promotion in mice; creatine causes hyperactive platelets in healthy humans
comments: Surprising pathological role for widely-used supplement; mechanistic link through non-canonical STAT5B phosphorylation is novel and actionable.

title: Oncogene inactivation-induced senescence facilitates tumor relapse
task: Establish oncogene inactivation-induced senescence as double-edged driver of tumor relapse
key_results: Oncogene inactivation rapidly induces senescence and pro-inflammatory SASP; predisposes to relapse with polyploidy, chromosomal instability, alternative oncogenic pathways (Mdm2 upregulation), neovascularization, and immunosuppressive TME shift; observed in BRAFV600E melanoma cells treated with vemurafenib
comments: Important clinical insight: senescence-inducing targeted therapies may simultaneously create permissive microenvironments for recurrence through SASP and immunosuppression.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Oncogene inactivation induces senescence and pro-inflammatory SASP

hypotheses.hypothesis: OIIS predisposes tumors to relapse through genomic instability and TME remodeling
hypotheses.result: Relapsed tumors exhibit polyploidy, CIN, alternative oncogenic pathways, and shift to immunosuppressive microenvironment

title: The SIRT5-SUCLG2 desuccinylation axis delays ovarian aging via a mitochondrial-epigenetic regulatory mechanism

comments: Mechanistically sophisticated mito-nuclear crosstalk model; connects mitochondrial metabolism to histone acetylation and senescence.

title: Direct coupling of nod factor signaling to vesicular trafficking initiates legume nodulation

title: Multiscale Modeling of Embryonic Morphogenesis from Fertilization to Organogenesis
task: Review multiscale modeling approaches for embryonic morphogenesis
key_results: Computational frameworks applied across molecular, cellular, and tissue scales to investigate patterning and form generation from fertilization to organogenesis
comments: Comprehensive review synthesizing diverse models across systems; lacks specific quantitative validation benchmarks.

title: Lysosomes and lysosomal dysfunction in ageing biology
task: Review lysosomes as hallmark and driver of aging pathology
key_results: Aging lysosomes show impaired biogenesis, defective acidification, reduced hydrolytic activity, and compromised membrane integrity; defects impair clearance of damaged organelles/macromolecules and promote stress responses, inflammageing, and senescence; linked to neurodegeneration, cardiometabolic disorders, and infection susceptibility
comments: Comprehensive review positioning lysosomes as central integrators of aging; therapeutic targeting of lysosomal dysfunction emerges as key geroprotective strategy.

title: Metabolite glues as a means of purine sensing and chemotherapeutic response
task: Establish metabolite glues as endogenous purine sensing and chemotherapeutic response mechanism
key_results: Purine nucleotides act as molecular glues tethering PPAT (rate-limiting purine biosynthesis enzyme) to NUDT5 inhibitor, enabling purine-level sensing and feedback control; thiopurine chemotherapeutics glue same complex with distinct orientations for enhanced function; metabolite-glue pocket adjusts conformation for variable compound binding
comments: Novel concept of endogenous metabolite glues as nutrient sensing mechanism; elegant mechanistic explanation for thiopurine efficacy and therapeutic potential of manipulating metabolite-protein interactions.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Purine nucleotides serve as molecular glues enabling PPAT-NUDT5 complex formation for feedback sensing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed with structural and biochemical characterization of metabolite-glue mechanism

hypotheses.hypothesis: Thiopurine chemotherapeutics exploit metabolite-glue pocket plasticity for enhanced potency
hypotheses.result: Thiopurines glue PPAT-NUDT5 in distinct orientations with greater potency; metabolite-glue pocket accommodates structural variations

title: ESCRT-III assembles around mis-segregated DNA to protect genome stability
task: Establish ESCRT-III-mediated DNA protection mechanism at mis-segregated DNA bridges
key_results: ESCRT-III transfers from reforming nuclear envelope to ultrafine DNA bridges upon Aurora B-dependent abscission checkpoint; CHMP1B/IST1 form double-stranded filaments encasing DNA and nucleosomes, preventing nuclease digestion and cGAS recognition; CHMP1B DNA-binding mutant causes cytokinesis failure and binucleation
comments: Elegant functional switch of ESCRT-III from nuclear envelope sealing to DNA protection; directly demonstrates ESCRT-III DNA-binding and protective capacity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: NoCut surveillance repurposes ESCRT-III from nuclear envelope to mis-segregated DNA bridges

title: Multiparametric analysis of sperm chromatin and ROS reveals the existence of subpopulations that are linked to embryo development after ICSI
